name: Polaris Ab
tagline: An compánach a d'athin Hubble — abhac grianach trí ghil an Chéiféide.

facts.label: Fithis
facts.value: ~18 AU from Polaris A — ~30-year period, e≈0.61

facts.label: Réiteach
facts.value: Separated only by Hubble's ACS — 0.17″ at closest

facts.label: Córas
facts.value: Triple — Ab orbits inside, B a wide 18″ companion

history: Polaris Ab is the North Star's hidden partner — a sunlike F6 dwarf whipping around the famous Cepheid on a steep e≈0.61 ellipse every ~30 years, so close it was only ever resolved by Hubble in 2006. Its swing period feeds back into the Cepheid's measured properties: Polaris's light pulse, mass and distance are being re-tuned by the companion's wobble. A third star, Polaris B, sails far wider at about 18 arcseconds — the telescopic double of the same system.
source: Evans et al. — HST/ACS resolution (2006) · CHARA orbit
